articles.title: A Pairing Hour on Free-Model Review: Three Dead Ends and the Two-Run Citation Filter
articles.excerpt: A 214-line backfill migration sat in review for two days. The junior engineer on the pairing rotation had already tried the obvious thing: paste the file into a free model and ask for a review. The re…
articles.body: A 214-line backfill migration sat in review for two days. The junior engineer on the pairing rotation had already tried the obvious thing: paste the file into a free model and ask for a review. The reply was a full rewrite of the file, formatted as a diff, with no mention of the one line that mattered — a new NOT NULL column read before its backfill ran. That was the first dead end of the hour. Three more followed before the session settled on something worth keeping: a review packet small enough to re-read, a rubric made of binary questions, and a two-run citation filter that discards every finding the model cannot point at. A note on evidence before any code. Every script below is runnable as written.

articles.excerpt: Arquiteturas baseadas em operações CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) colapsam invariavelmente sob concorrência extrema. Quando uma corporação acopla fluxos transacionais de alta velocidade e consult…
articles.body: Arquiteturas baseadas em operações CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) colapsam invariavelmente sob concorrência extrema. Quando uma corporação acopla fluxos transacionais de alta velocidade e consultas de agregação na mesma modelagem relacional, o motor de banco de dados sofre contenção severa. Bloqueios de linha para garantir a consistência de gravações paralisam as leituras, enquanto consultas analíticas bloqueiam as mutações essenciais de negócios. A adoção simultânea dos padrões CQRS e Event Sourcing dissolve este antipadrão estrutural. Ao desmantelar o modelo de dados unificado, engenheiros separam fisicamente as operações que alteram o estado (Commands) das operações que retornam informações (Queries).

articles.title: Verified, then swapped: two supply-chain attacks on the code you didn't write
articles.excerpt: On 4 November 2026, two unrelated reports landed on the same day. In the morning, Debian, Ubuntu and the developers of APT, the program that installs software on both systems, published fixes for a fl…
articles.body: On 4 November 2026, two unrelated reports landed on the same day. In the morning, Debian, Ubuntu and the developers of APT, the program that installs software on both systems, published fixes for a flaw that let an attacker on the network swap a package after it had passed its signature check . The attacker's code then ran as root. A few hours later, the French security firm Sekoia described a campaign it links to the Russian group APT29. For one week, a small web analytics script loaded by thousands of websites quietly added a second script that profiled every visitor's phone and served it an exploit chain to match. One story is about servers, the other about websites.
articles.author: Sentinelleai

articles.title: Map the Blast Radius Before the Review: A Per-Symbol Ledger for Small OSS Patches
articles.excerpt: A four-line patch, two approvals, and a retry that never fires A small project ships a four-line change to an error-handling branch late on a Friday afternoon. Two reviewers read the diff, both approv…
articles.body: A four-line patch, two approvals, and a retry that never fires A small project ships a four-line change to an error-handling branch late on a Friday afternoon. Two reviewers read the diff, both approve it, and the patch merges with a green CI run. Three weeks later a downstream consumer reports a retry loop that never fires, and the root cause sits in a caller nobody re-read. That story is a composite illustration rather than a logged incident, but it captures a real tension in small-maintainer projects: review attention is scarce and the diff is the only surface anyone inspects. Whole-repository review prompts do not fix this, because they spend effort rescanning untouched code.
articles.author: Blake Yang

articles.title: Building an Evidence Trail for CVE-2026-76466 Remediation
articles.excerpt: Building an Evidence Trail for CVE-2026-76466 Remediation The CVE-2026-76466 advisory names a clear outcome: unauthenticated remote command execution as root. It also names conditions that are easy to…
articles.body: Building an Evidence Trail for CVE-2026-76466 Remediation The CVE-2026-76466 advisory names a clear outcome: unauthenticated remote command execution as root. It also names conditions that are easy to lose in a large patch program: Cisco Expressway clustering and TLS Verify Mode. A remediation record should make those conditions auditable. Cisco published the advisory on October 21, 2026, with a CVSS 3.1 score of 9.8. The affected releases are X14 and earlier, plus X15.5.3 and earlier. The first fixed X15 release is X15.5.20. X14 and earlier must migrate to a fixed release. Cisco lists no workaround. Record the scope before the change Create one record per cluster and list every Expressway-C and Expressway-E member.

articles.excerpt: 📅 November 7, 2026 • Uber Engineering Secure AI, the defense-in-depth framework it uses to protect AI agents in production, in a post dated November 6, 2026. The framework has three layers: provision…
articles.body: 📅 November 7, 2026 • Uber Engineering Uber published Secure AI , the defense-in-depth framework it uses to protect AI agents in production, in a post dated November 6, 2026 . The framework has three layers: provisioning-time validation, runtime enforcement and continuous assurance. Per Uber, identity and authorization remain necessary but stop being sufficient once software reasons over untrusted content, picks tools on its own and acts on a user's behalf. From access control to behavior control Uber says agentic systems need a semantic layer that answers not only whether an agent may act, but whether it should act given the request, the agent's purpose and the session so far.

articles.body: When the Mass Effect Legendary Edition came out in 2021, it included the single player campaign of all three original games, along with all the DLC. But while all the story content you could ever want was included, Mass Effect 3's multiplayer mode was conspicuously absent, despite having a dedicated fanbase. Now, just a few weeks after EA's shutdown of BioWare , a team of modders has successfully ported Mass Effect 3 's multiplayer to the Legendary Edition, with all the graphics and engine improvements that came with that re-release. The mod will be coming out on N7 Day – November 7th – and will be free to play, as long as you already own Mass Effect Legendary Edition.

articles.excerpt: Over the past few months, there's been a sort of explosion of AI in the modding scene. Whether it's mashup mods on Twitter or full decompilation done by Claude, AI is everywhere in the mod community,…
articles.body: Over the past few months, there's been an explosion of AI in the modding scene. Whether it's mashup mods on Twitter or full decompilation done by Claude , AI is everywhere in the mod community, and it could be killing the hobby. I got a chance to sit down with ME3Tweaks' Mgamerz to talk about his new Mass Effect Legendary Edition ME3 Multiplayer mod, where I asked him about how AI has affected the modding community. While he admits that Claude is very effective at modding games, it's causing an avalanche of low-effort content that's hard to sift through. And, while there has always been a range of quality for mods, the inherent difficulty of getting into a game's files and changing things was a natural filter that's slowly eroding.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission, the first Mars mission in 20 years. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years! The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner , Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water. Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites. Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected.

articles.body: We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission. Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027. The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034.

articles.title: 'I think we will prevail': NASA chief Jared Isaacman on Artemis, China and the new moon race (exclusive)
articles.excerpt: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman during a a Dec. 3, 2025 confirmation hearing. In October of 2026, Isaacman sat down with Space.com to discuss the future of the space agency.
articles.body: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman is serious about launching "big rockets" to the moon every single year for the agency's Artemis program. And the new space race with China is fueling that ambition. "I feel good. I feel like we are certainly on a more achievable path to the lunar surface today than where we were before," Isaacman told Space.com. We recently sat down with the NASA chief to discuss the state of the Artemis program , and, off the bat, he made it clear that he's confident in the U.S. space program following the success of April's Artemis II mission around the moon. In fact, just prior to our conversation, it was announced that Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman will become the new deputy director of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory.

articles.title: SpaceX launches mystery mission for US Space Force in gorgeous sunset liftoff from California (video, photos)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force from California this evening (Nov. 6). It was the company's 125th liftoff of 2026.
articles.body: SpaceX just launched a classified mission for the U.S. military. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base this evening (Nov. 6) at 7:48 p.m. EST (4:48 p.m. local California time; 0048 GMT on Nov. 7), rising into the sky as the sun sank toward the Pacific. The launch kicked off the USSF-432 mission for the U.S. Space Force , which we know little about. Neither SpaceX nor the Space Force told us much about USSF-432 beforehand, and we learned tonight; SpaceX cut its webcast off about 10 minutes into the flight, shortly after the Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth for a landing. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the USSF-432 mission for the U.S. Space Force from Vandenberg Space Force Base on Nov. 6, 2026.
